Rejected Stone
ree-JEK-tid stohn
noun
From Psalm 118:22; the stone which the builders refused, become the head of the corner—a figure of Christ.

📖 Biblical Definition

The rejected stone is the figure of Psalm 118, taken up by Christ and the apostles as a prophecy of His rejection and exaltation: The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner. This is the LORD’s doing; it is marvellous in our eyes. The builders are the rulers of Israel, who examined the living Stone and cast Him away as unfit, crucifying the Lord of glory; yet the very stone they rejected God made the head of the corner, the chief and indispensable stone that binds the whole building together. The Lord applied the psalm to Himself before His enemies: Did ye never read in the scriptures, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner? Peter preached it to the rulers: This is the stone which was set at nought of you builders, which is become the head of the corner; neither is there salvation in any other. The same Stone is precious to believers but, to the disobedient, a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence, on which they fall and are broken. The dictionary honors the rejected stone as a great prophecy of Christ crucified and risen—refused by men, exalted by God, the head of the corner and the only foundation of salvation—and a solemn warning, that the Stone men reject in unbelief becomes the rock on which they are finally broken.

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The prophecy is reduced to a tale of unlikely success; Scripture proclaims Christ rejected by men and exalted by God, precious to faith and a stumbling-stone to unbelief.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The corruption is the flattening of the prophecy into a mere proverb of unlikely success—the underdog vindicated, the overlooked one who rises—detached from its true subject, Christ crucified and risen. The psalm is no general maxim; it is a specific prophecy of the Messiah whom Israel’s builders examined and refused, and whom God exalted as the head of the corner. This is the Lord’s doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes (Matt 21:42).

The principle to recover is the double significance of the rejected Stone. To those who believe He is precious, the chief corner stone, the sure foundation, the head that binds the whole building—and neither is there salvation in any other, for this is the stone set at nought of the builders, become the head of the corner (Acts 4:11). But to the disobedient the same Stone is a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence (1 Pet 2:7-8): they reject Him in unbelief, and on the very Stone they refuse they are at last broken. So the rejected Stone is both the only foundation of salvation and the rock of judgment; what men do with Him in rejection or faith determines whether He is their corner stone or their stumbling stone.
